# Bubbles managed Python dependencies.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# --------------------
# bubbles/scripts/dependency-posture.sh declares python3 + PyYAML + jsonschema
# REQUIRED ("a guard that skips is a guard that lies"), but the framework
# shipped no supported way to obtain them. Every operator and every agent
# session therefore invented its own shortcut — `pip install
# --break-system-packages`, or a throwaway virtualenv under /tmp that vanishes
# on reboot and is referenced by nothing. This file plus
# bubbles/scripts/python-env.sh replace those shortcuts with one reproducible
# provisioning path.
#
# Provision with:
#   bash bubbles/scripts/python-env.sh --provision
#
# SOURCE LOCKING
# --------------
# Exactly one explicit index. No --extra-index-url, no implicit fall-through.
# This mirrors the build-time source-locking rule the framework ships to
# downstream repos in instructions/bubbles-supply-chain-source-locking.instructions.md.
--index-url https://pypi.org/simple

# HASH PINNING — DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED DEVIATION
# -----------------------------------------------
# The shipped source-locking instruction asks for hash-pinned
# (`--require-hashes`) requirements. That is NOT applied here, and the reason is
# recorded rather than hidden:
#
#   `--require-hashes` needs a hash for every artifact actually installed.
#   PyYAML and rpds-py ship platform-specific binary wheels (rpds-py is a Rust
#   extension), so a hash set captured on macOS/arm64 would refuse to install on
#   the Linux CI leg, and sdist-only installation would require a Rust toolchain
#   on every machine. A cross-platform hash set is regenerable, but it must be
#   regenerated per platform per bump or it silently becomes the thing that
#   blocks CI.
#
# What IS locked: a single explicit index, and an exact `==` pin on the COMPLETE
# dependency closure (direct and transitive), so a resolve is reproducible for a
# given platform. Revisit hash pinning if this set ever becomes pure-Python.

# --- direct ---
PyYAML==6.0.3
jsonschema==4.26.0

# --- transitive closure of jsonschema, pinned so resolution is reproducible ---
attrs==26.1.0
jsonschema-specifications==2025.9.1
referencing==0.37.0
rpds-py==2026.6.3
